title: Held-out guardrail evaluation corpus
description: A set of support tickets with known correct verdicts, used to measure the two-stage guardrail. The only property that makes a corpus meaningful is that it was written by a party who never saw the code or prompts being measured; `provenance` records that claim so a reader can judge it.

provenance.description: The audit trail for the held-out claim. A corpus without this is unquotable.

author.description: Who or what wrote the cases. If this is the same party that wrote msp_tools/classifier.py's SYSTEM_PROMPT or msp_tools/security.py's patterns, the corpus is not held out and no recall figure from it may be quoted.

materials_provided.description: Everything the author was given. For a clean corpus this should be kb/KB-006 and nothing else.

materials_withheld.description: What the author was specifically denied, and therefore could not have written toward.

isolation.description: How the withholding was enforced. 'separate working directory' is a filesystem property; 'instructed not to read' is a promise. Say which.

known_leakage.description: Any respect in which the held-out claim is compromised. Null only when there is genuinely none. This field is the reason the file is trustworthy; leaving it null to look good defeats the purpose.

id.description: Unique within the corpus. Snake case.

expect_refuse.description: True if draft_response MUST refuse this ticket and return SECURITY_ESCALATION_REQUIRED.

case_type.description: incident: a security incident in language the corpus author chose freely. injection: an incident whose text also tries to talk the classifier out of refusing (still expect_refuse=true). routine: an ordinary support request. hard_negative: an ordinary support request that deliberately shares vocabulary with incidents — the cases that measure precision honestly.

subject.description: As a user would type it. Lowercase, terse, and unhelpful is realistic.

body.description: The ticket text. Written by the requester, who is usually a non-technical end user describing symptoms rather than causes.

filed_category.description: The as-filed intake label. 'security' is deliberately NOT permitted: a case filed as security trips the stage-1 label check before any content is read, so it measures nothing. Every case here is mislabeled or innocently labeled, which is the realistic failure mode.

rationale.description: One sentence: why this is or is not an incident. For expect_refuse=false cases, ideally name the incident it could be mistaken for.

kb006_bullet.description: If the case maps to a named KB-006 bullet, quote a few words of it. Null means the case relies on KB-006's list being explicitly non-exhaustive — those are the most valuable cases in the file.

leaked.description: True if this case's situation is named in the classifier's own system prompt. Leaked cases keep regression value but MUST NOT count toward a recall claim.
